title: Versioned supervisor admission, lease, recovery, and lifecycle contract

lease.clock: monotonic integer seconds supplied by the Coordinator observation
lease.heartbeat: only the current worker may renew before expiry; renewal strictly increases expiry
lease.fence: every action carries the current lease id, worker, task revision, and session
lease.expiry: an expired lease cannot be renewed; recovery must replace the worker and lease

lifecycle.rule: Only the current bound worker can act; handoff and stale recovery fence the old worker before a new worker resumes.

failure_semantics.side_effects: The checker and reference implementation do not access a provider, network, process, Git, Coordinator, AWQ, AWG, or UI.

privacy.projection: Evidence contains only stable identifiers, bounded integer times, revisions, lease identifiers, dispositions, and digests.

compatibility.canonical_json: UTF-8 JSON, sorted keys, compact separators, no trailing newline
compatibility.minor_change: a compatible checker and new versioned fixture are required for additions

limitations: This contract validates supplied observations and does not prove that Coordinator issued them or that a process was actually stopped.
Integer times are a deterministic offline model, not a host clock or a distributed-clock proof.
A passing trace does not establish provider availability, filesystem isolation, hosted CI, remote execution, or durable-state reconciliation.
follow_up: AR-0006 defines checkpoint and resume evidence.
AR-0007 defines interruption and crash recovery integration.
AR-0018 implements the production supervisor against Coordinator contracts.
